rules: one fixed renderer for all words and arms
per consonant, in SOURCE order, emit BOTH binding and liberating rows (fixed dual-pole schema)
NEVER choose polarity per word; NEVER paraphrase rows per word (identical paraphrase table across words); NO bespoke prose synthesis
preserve packet length (feature count == consonant count)
NO consonant symbol, NO Devanāgarī, NO IAST in the rendered packet (leakage block)

EVALUATOR-FACING render is ENGLISH-ONLY: strip/paraphrase every Sanskrit vṛtti proper-name (e.g. 'avajñā', 'kruratā', 'karuṇā') so no source-language term that could be reverse-mapped to a consonant appears; authored blind at the packet-authoring-and-freeze step and hash-pinned
identical formatting across words and arms
row order fixed to source order; order tested only via the secondary S / O arms
raw_mapped_rows_note: the SET manifests freeze the RAW mapped rows (provenance). The evaluator-facing English-only render is a fixed, blind, table-driven paraphrase of those rows, authored + frozen at the next step (that is why readiness is PACKET_AUTHORING_AND_FREEZE).

example_raw_packet_bala.binding: avajñā — neglect / disregard of what actually has value; indifference misapplied so that genuine worth goes unattended
example_raw_packet_bala.liberating: regard that recognizes and attends to worth — giving due attention to what has value (and reserving indifference/upekṣā only for the truly unacceptable)

example_raw_packet_bala.binding: kruratā — cruelty: physical harm inflicted on the weak; crude, cruel thought and behaviour
example_raw_packet_bala.liberating: compassion (karuṇā) that protects the vulnerable — the counter-measure to cruelty; the will to reduce another's misery and help arouse their latent intellect

leakage_guarantee: evaluator sees English-only descriptive vṛtti content; NO consonant symbol, NO Sanskrit vṛtti proper-name, NO spelling — identity is never directly shown
